default.notes: A short-stay visa (type C) from a Bosnian embassy or consulate is required. Holders of a valid multiple-entry Schengen visa can instead enter visa-free for up to 30 days within the visa's validity.

groups.notes: Visa-free for up to 90 days in any 180-day period; EU and EEA citizens can enter with a national ID card instead of a passport.
Visa-free for up to 90 days in any 180-day period, in line with the EU's visa-free list.
Visa-free for up to 90 days in any 180-day period; citizens of neighbouring Balkan states can generally also cross with a national ID card.
Visa-free for up to 90 days in any 180-day period under bilateral agreements.
Gulf state citizens can visit visa-free for up to 90 days in any 180-day period.

BA.notes: Home country — no entry requirements for citizens of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

RU.notes: Russian citizens can enter visa-free for up to 30 days per visit under the bilateral agreement — longer stays require a visa or residence grounds.

UA.notes: Ukrainian citizens can enter visa-free for short stays — commonly quoted as up to 30 days per visit under the bilateral agreement; confirm with a Bosnian mission before a longer trip.

XK.notes: Bosnia and Herzegovina does not recognise Kosovo, and Kosovo passport holders have generally needed a visa — check current arrangements with a Bosnian mission before travel.
